paragraphs.text: “Joshua.” Heb., Yehoh·shuʹaʽ, “Jehoshua,” meaning “Jehovah Is Salvation”; Gr., Ἰησοῖ (I·e·soiʹ, “Jesus”); Sy, “Jeshua”; Vgc, “Josue.” See Ge 49:18 ftn, “You”; Heb 4:8 ftn, “Joshua.”
“Let there be a remembering.” In Heb. this is a verb in the infinitive absolute, indefinite as to time and impersonal.
Or, “courage.” Heb., ruʹach; Gr., pneuʹma; Lat., spiʹri·tus.
About 890 m (2,920 ft). Compare Ac 1:12 ftn.
“A living God.” Heb., ʼEl, followed by the sing. adjective chai, “living”; Gr., The·osʹ zon; Lat., Deʹus viʹvens.
“Lord of.” Heb., ʼAdhohnʹ, sing.; Gr., Ky·riʹou; Lat., Doʹmi·ni. Contrast De 10:17.

Generally identified with Tell ed-Damiyeh, on the east bank of the Jordan River, 29 km (18 mi) north of Jericho. History records similar blockages of the Jordan by landslides in 1267 C.E. and in 1927 C.E.
Lit., “daggers (swords) of rock.” Heb., cha·revohthʹ tsu·rimʹ.
“Hill of the Foreskins,” Vg; LXX, “the place called Hill (Mound) of the Foreskins.”
Or, “but I—⁠as chief of the army of Jehovah.” Heb., ki ʼaniʹ sar-tsevaʼ-Yehwahʹ.
“Going round.” In Heb. this is a verb in the infinitive absolute, indefinite as to time.
“With a continual blowing.” In Heb. these words are two verbs in the infinitive absolute, indefinite as to time.
“For fear you may get a desire,” in harmony with LXX, which reads: “that, setting your mind on [it], (you yourselves may not take)”; M, “for fear you may devote [it] to destruction.”
“Achan.” Heb., ʽA·khanʹ; in 1Ch 2:7, “Achar,” both meaning “Trouble; Troubler.” See 1Ch 2:7 ftns.
One of 134 scribal changes from YHWH to ʼAdho·naiʹ. See App 1B.
Lit., “by the able-bodied men.” Heb., lag·geva·rimʹ; Gr., ka·taʹ anʹdra, used in the distributive sense; SyVgc and six Heb. mss, “household by household.”
“The stake.” Lit., “the tree (wood).” Heb., ha·ʽetsʹ; Gr., xyʹlou; Lat., cruʹce.
“A copy of.” Heb., mish·nehʹ; Gr., deu·te·ro·noʹmi·on. See De 1:1 ftn, “Words.”
“The congregation of.” Heb., qehalʹ; Gr., ek·kle·siʹas.
“Letting . . . live.” In Heb. this is a verb in the infinitive absolute, indefinite as to time and impersonal.
“For our souls (lives).” Heb., lenaph·sho·thehʹnu; Gr., psy·khonʹ; Lat., a·ni·maʹbus.
“Accordingly . . . [he] constituted them.” Lit., “And [he] gave them.” Heb., wai·yit·tenemʹ (from na·thanʹ, from which the word “Nethinim” is derived).
“They,” TLagardianSy; M, “he,” in the collective sense, referring to “Israel”; Gr., Kyʹri·os, “Jehovah.”
Lit., “trees.” Gr., xyʹlon; Lat., stiʹpi·tes, “posts; tree trunks.”
“Every soul.” Heb., kol-han·neʹphesh; Gr., pan em·pneʹon, “everything breathing.”
Lit., “every breath.” Gr., pan em·pneʹon zo·esʹ, “every breather of life”; Vg, “everything that could breathe.”
“Devoting [them] to destruction.” In Heb. this is a verb in the infinitive absolute, indefinite as to time and impersonal.
Probably Jiljulieh, north of the brook Kanah, near the plain of Sharon. LXX, “Galilee.”
“Axis lords of.” Heb., sar·nehʹ, used only with reference to the Philistines. Taken from the Heb. root word seʹren, “axle; axis,” as in 1Ki 7:30.

Or, “people of Gebal.” In Eze 27:9 (LXX), they are called Biblians, inhabitants of Byblos, a city that was prominent for making papyrus into paper for writing material. In time bi·bliʹa came to describe various writings, scrolls, books and eventually the collection of little books that make up the Bible.
Possibly, “as far as Lebi-hamath (Lion of Hamath),” the name of a place. See VT, Vol. II, 1952, p. 114.
“To the half tribe of.” Heb., la·chatsiʹ sheʹvet (tribe).
“Of the half tribe of.” Heb., la·chatsiʹ mat·tehʹ (“tribe,” used interchangeably with sheʹvet).
“Was the city of Arbok [LXXB, “Argob”], this being the metropolis of the Anakim,” LXX.
“Valley of Hinnom.” Heb., gheh-Hin·nomʹ; LXXA(Gr.), phaʹrag·gos En·nomʹ; Lat., Ge·henʹnom. See App 4C.
Or, “Then she slid down (alighted) from off the ass.”
Or, “the upper basin and the lower basin.”
Lit., “the sea of the border; the bordering sea.” MmarginLXXSyVg, “the Great Sea.”
“A lot,” inserted for sense. Lit., “it,” referring to “the lot” in vs 1.
“Valley of Hinnom.” Heb., geh Hin·nomʹ; Gr., Gaiʹen·na; Lat., Ge·henʹnom. From this comes the English word “Gehenna.” See App 4C.
Lit., “which was marked out to Neah.”
“In the region of Achzib.” Possibly, “and to Meheleb and Achzib.” LXXB, “and toward Leb and Echozob.”
“And to Judah at the Jordan.” Possibly, “and by the banks of the Jordan,” by a slight correction of M proposed by C. F. Houbigant; LXX, “and the Jordan.” Compare 3:15.
Lit., “And the territory of the sons of Dan went on out (got away; was lost) from them.”
Lit., “the great priest,” M; Lat., sa·cerʹdos maʹgnus.
Or, “in the circuit.” Heb., bag·Ga·lilʹ; Gr., Ga·li·laiʹai; Lat., Ga·li·leʹa. “Galilee” later designated the Roman province north of Samaria.
According to M; LXXSyVg, “out of the tribe of.”

Vss 36, 37 are according to some Heb. mss, LXXSyVgc and 1Ch 6:63, 78, 79 (Sy names these four cities after vs 34); Al, Ca and Leningrad B 19A omit vss 36, 37, apparently due to a scribal error made because vss 35, 37 both end with “four cities.”

Or, “The God of gods, Jehovah, the God of gods, Jehovah.” Heb., ʼEl ׀ ʼElo·himʹ ׀ Yehwahʹ, ʼEl ׀ ʼElo·himʹ ׀ Yehwahʹ, with the dividing stroke (pa·seqʹ) between the words. This expression ʼEl ʼElo·himʹ Yehwahʹ occurs, unrepeated, in Ps 50:1. Lat., For·tisʹsi·mus Deʹus Doʹmi·nus, For·tisʹsi·mus Deʹus Doʹmi·nus, “The Most Mighty God Jehovah, The Most Mighty God Jehovah.” The first word, ʼEl, of the Heb. expression we have rendered “Divine One.” It may also be rendered “God; Mighty One.”
“Rebellion,” M. Gr., a·po·sta·siʹai, “apostasy,” from the verb a·phiʹste·mi, “stand away from”; the noun has the sense of “desertion; abandonment; rebellion.” See 2Ch 29:19; Ac 21:21; 2Th 2:3 ftns.
Or, “What do you have in common with Jehovah?” Lit., “What [is there] to you and to Jehovah?” A Heb. idiom; a repellent question indicating an objection. See App 7B.
Or, “feature of worship.” Heb., ʽavo·dhathʹ; Gr., la·treiʹan, “sacred service.” Compare Ex 3:12 ftn.
From the explanation given, the altar was likely named Witness. Sy adds, “the altar of witness.”
Lit., “I caused to fall to (for) you.” LXX, “I cast upon you”; Vg, “he divided to you by lot.”
Lit., “these nations that remain as an inheritance for your tribes from the Jordan, and all the [other] nations that I cut off.”
“For your souls (lives; selves).” Heb., lenaph·sho·theh·khemʹ, pl.; Syr., benaph·shekhun.
“And they used to serve (worship).” Heb., wai·ya·ʽav·dhuʹ; Gr., e·laʹtreu·san, “they rendered sacred service.” See Ex 3:12 ftn.
“Other gods.” Heb., ʼelo·himʹ ʼache·rimʹ, both pl.
“With what [things],” LXXB; LXXA, “with the signs that”; M, “just as.”
The expression ‘to send the feeling of dejection’ is also found in Ex 23:28 and De 7:20. See Ex 23:28 ftn.
That is, east of the Euphrates River.

Lit., “He [is] a holy God.” Heb., ʼElo·himʹ qedho·shimʹ huʼ. Although modified by a pl. adjective, the sing. pronoun huʼ shows ʼElo·himʹ is pl. to denote majesty and excellence, hence, sing. in sense. Gr., The·osʹ; Lat., Deʹus.
“Pieces of money.” Heb., qesi·tahʹ, the value of which is uncertain.
Or, “in Gibeah of Phinehas”; in agreement with LXXVg.
